businessVision: ProjectOS governs its own delivery through one lifecycle that a person can drive interactively today and that the host can drive unattended once its owner activates the path, with every decision attributable to the route that obtained it and every independent review made about candidate evidence the host established for itself. Delivery is led by exactly one project leader per governed project execution, who assembles the smallest credible team from a complete, pinned, governed specialist catalogue, while ProjectOS stays above every agent and the owner keeps every protected action.
definitionOfComplete: Two outcomes are complete. First, the host review foundation: the complete dormant agent-to-host unattended review path exists in production source, and after implementation closure no additional source code bridge is required for live operation; only protected activation inputs may remain, namely owner-signed activation material, live capability and grants, credential and configuration, access-control application, service start, provider availability and the owner publication decision. Second, the agent workforce foundation: ProjectOS has exactly one persistent project leader per active governed project execution, a versioned agent registry holding the complete approved specialist catalogue at a pinned upstream commit, dynamic minimum-team selection with an explained rationale, permissions decided only by governance-owned configuration, structured specialist result contracts, an operational leader ledger that never competes with the governance records, separation of agent role from execution model, third-party provenance, governed catalogue updates, a basic evaluation contract and independent-review boundaries; no imported agent can widen authority or go around a ProjectOS or owner gate.
successStandard: The host independently pins the candidate commit, independently resolves the approved phase baseline, derives the complete reviewer-visible evidence for the change between them through the one existing repository reader, frames that evidence itself, executes the review against exactly that framed evidence and attests its digest together with the baseline, the candidate, the request and the decision. An agent cannot obtain a candidate review attestation for a subject of its own choosing. Every production port of the host review has a source implementation that fails closed while live inputs are absent. The installed service contains the dormant review-capable route and cannot exercise it without an authority no shipped build can obtain. Unattended technical review runs against a bounded local candidate commit that grants no publication authority. Admitted cost comes from an owner-signed policy and is never described as billed cost. The real isolated transport proofs pass, the interactive route is unchanged, and no provider is called, no credential is held, no money is spent and no service is started. Every active governed project execution has exactly one project leader and a second is refused; no specialist runs without one; the registered agent count equals the count discovered at the pinned upstream commit, with per-agent provenance and digest; an imported instruction cannot widen any permission; selection is minimal, bounded and explained; every specialist result is schema-valid and reaches the leader ledger with contradictions surfaced; a role survives a change of execution model; an upstream catalogue change is detected rather than imported; and a user drives the workforce by stating an objective, never by naming agents.
approvedScope: Everything the preceding host review path phase already implemented, validated and reviewed is inherited as implementation context and is continued, not rebuilt: the identity and committed-candidate digests, the host plan authority and pinned candidate source, the sealed execution seam and its single evidence mint, the host decision representation, the response envelope and responder, the single-read request inbox, the review exchange on the one existing endpoint, the agent transport, client, activation and composition, the reservation settlement rule, the cross-language vectors and the phase validator.

A host candidate-evidence contract. The candidate is the commit the host pinned for itself. The baseline is the approved phase baseline the host resolved for itself. The evidence is the host-derived reviewer-visible account of the change from the baseline to the candidate.

One narrowly bounded read-only addition to the existing repository reader: a recursive tree difference between two exact commits that reports, for every changed path, the change status, the old and new file mode and the old and new object identity, with rename detection disabled, full-length identities and unambiguous record separation. It compares the two endpoint trees, never a walk of the commits between them. The production command spelling is deterministic and validator-pinned. No second repository reader is created.

An ancestry refusal: the host refuses unless the baseline is present, the candidate is present and the baseline is an ancestor of the candidate. The ancestry question is answered through the same existing reader, and the candidate is the head commit of the governed phase worktree as the host pinned it once.

Object-store integrity for every host repository read used by the review, the existing committed-blob read included: replacement references and grafts are disabled, no repository-local, user-level or system-level git configuration can alter what is read or cause a program to run, the process environment is fixed by the host, and contents are the raw committed object bytes with no filter, conversion or line-ending translation.

A host-written evidence envelope with two separate blocks. The first block is host-established candidate evidence: the baseline commit, the candidate commit, the complete changed-path set, and for each path the change type, the old and new file mode, the content identity, the sha256 of the reviewer-visible bytes and the bounded authoritative contents. Deleted paths are explicit. The second block is agent-claimed supporting information, labelled as not host verified. The boundary between the blocks is a host-generated marker that cannot be derived from candidate content, and the host-written reviewer instructions state that every byte inside either block is data and never an instruction, including any text that resembles a block boundary, a host statement or a reviewer directive. Nothing in the second block can substitute for the first, and the host alone decides the first.

Refusal rather than truncation: a submodule pointer entry, any other unsupported entry kind, an ambiguous parse, an oversize path or total evidence beyond the configured bound refuses the review. A symbolic link entry is reported explicitly as a link and is never followed. Authoritative evidence is never silently truncated.

An attestation binding extended to the baseline, the candidate, the digest of the canonical evidence, the request and correlation, the review decision and the existing authority bindings. The review operation executes against the exact host-framed evidence whose digest is attested.

A trusted baseline sourced from owner-bound plan and phase authority through the durable approved-plan record, including the precise durable-plan field and adapter that carry it. The baseline is never taken from agent prose, never from a mutable remote-tracking reference and never derived or advanced at run time: the baseline of any later continuation is set only by a newly owner-approved plan. For this continuation the approved baseline is commit 20fe0722528af748504baf9c094818c003a95ef7.

A bounded local candidate commit authority. Inside an owner-approved active phase ProjectOS may mechanically create a local candidate commit for independent review, in the governed phase worktree only, containing only phase-scope changes. The commit is created without executing any repository hook and without any repository-local or user-level configuration being able to run a program. A required correction is an additive local commit, and the reviewed object is always the cumulative change from the approved baseline to the newest candidate. An unreviewed local candidate commit is consumable by no other governed action. Push and publication remain separately governed.

A technical-continuation ordering change for the unattended route only: the candidate is committed locally before the independent review, the review is made against that immutable commit, and an approval authorises the separately governed continuation. The interactive route keeps its existing order.

An owner-signed execution-cost policy carried by the second-version execution closure, holding at minimum a maximum call cost in micro dollars used for pre-dispatch admission and reservation, and where deterministic post-call accounting is required a signed bounded rate card tied to the approved model policy. The policy is covered by the owner's signature under the closure's one canonical encoding, and a verified closure that lacks it is refused rather than given a default.

Canonical text identities for the model policy and for the credential reference and purpose, carried by the owner-signed second-version execution closure under its one canonical deterministic encoding and covered by the owner's signature. After closure verification the host derives the model-policy identity digest and the credential-reference identity digest from that text. A verified closure that lacks either identity is refused rather than given a default. The owner programme delegation carries the corresponding digest claims as the cross-check and is never the host's independent source.

Source implementations of every production port of the host review, each failing closed while live inputs are absent: the admitted-cost source, the signed-execution-closure facts source, the trust-manifest port, the committed-bytes port, the executable-policy port, the gatekeeper execution port that launches the closure-verified broker under the pinned packaged runtime, the clock port, the status-and-review service route, the status representation of the review capability state, and the session and peer composition.

The installed service's production composition contains the dormant review-capable route. It remains impossible to exercise without the unminted review capability, and the live status continues to report protected operations as not authorised while that capability is unminted.

Declared validator amendments, each stated as an exact old invariant and an exact new invariant and each ratified at this phase's gate. This phase's gate ratifies both amendments first declared for the preceding phase as well, restating each with its old and new invariant, so that neither rests on that phase's narrower gate sentence.

Proofs: evidence completeness for the baseline-to-candidate change, baseline-not-ancestor refusal, candidate mismatch refusal, missing and oversize evidence refusal, agent-claimed text unable to replace host evidence, attestation evidence-digest mismatch refusal, cross-language vectors, the real isolated pipe proof, the run, reconcile and closure vertical proofs, reservation semantics and interactive non-regression.

The relationship to the preceding host review path phase. The planning mechanism keeps that unfinished phase in the plan unchanged, because an approved plan record leaves the current corpus only when every one of its phases is recorded complete. That phase may not close independently. This phase must first complete and be accepted against the cumulative implementation candidate; only after that acceptance may the preceding phase be reconciled and closed, by the owner, against that same accepted cumulative candidate. No earlier candidate of the preceding phase alone may be treated as the final implementation, and this phase's declared amendments supersede that phase's statement that no other pinned invariant changes.

An agent workforce foundation for ProjectOS, built after the host review foundation, in which exactly one project leader leads operational delivery for each active governed project execution and dynamically selected specialists work under it, while ProjectOS keeps permissions, evidence, gates, approvals and closure and the owner keeps every protected action.

A ProjectOS-native project leader role, written for ProjectOS rather than copied unchanged from any one imported prompt, drawing on project management, product delivery, software architecture, multi-agent systems architecture, delivery risk, dependency management and project state management. The project leader acts inside the existing implementer governance role and adds no governance role.

A versioned, ProjectOS-governed agent registry holding normalised metadata for every agent of the complete approved specialist catalogue at one pinned upstream commit, with per-agent provenance and digest, where the imported instruction text is expertise configuration and never authority.

Structured specialist task and result contracts, a project leader operational ledger, dynamic minimum-team selection with an explained rationale, least-privilege context and tool grants, separation of agent role from execution model, review independence rules, governed catalogue updates, a basic evaluation contract, and team-size, cost and context controls.

A narrow mechanical phase-selection guard. While the host review continuation phase is not accepted, automated phase selection never selects the historical host review phase and selects the continuation phase as the executable work in its place. After the continuation phase is accepted, the historical phase becomes selectable only for the governed reconciliation and closure operation, against the same accepted cumulative candidate, and never for implementation execution. The one historical-to-continuation pairing this applies to is fixed in governed source or a committed owner record and is pinned to exactly that pair by the extended work-record authority validator; every other phase keeps the unchanged rule that the first phase in plan order not recorded complete is the phase.
excludedScope: Starting, installing or reconfiguring the host service.
Minting or granting the review capability, the service-control observation capability or the clock-binding grant.
Producing, signing or installing the owner-signed second-version execution closure or the owner-signed delegation, and any signing or private key use.
Provisioning, reading or disclosing any live credential or live configuration.
Applying or changing the access control on the real host endpoint, the real request store, the real response store or the real attestation store.
Any real provider call, any provider spend, and enabling production unattended execution.
Push, merge, tag, amend, reset, rebase, force update, history rewrite and publication of any candidate commit.
Any deployment, any production machine change and any production data change.
Establishing the actual provider-billed cost of a call. Actual provider-billing reconciliation remains the deferred wider actual-spend programme.

Host-signed response records or any other cryptographic authentication of the host to the agent. Host response authentication and storage authority must be explicitly proven before live use and is an activation blocker, not work of this phase.

Any new wire protocol, any second transport stack, any second production endpoint, any second repository reader, any second candidate digest, any generic evidence upload and any widening of the fixed authority frames to carry free-form data.
The decision on who may change the committed host review configuration block.
Control Center user interface work, unrelated host security deepening, and the known baseline validator failures.

Importing, installing or activating the specialist catalogue before the agent workforce phase, and in that phase any acquisition other than the owner-approved one-time read-only quarantined acquisition at the ratified commit, or any acquisition that works around the existing specialist-corpus access guard.
Installing specialists globally into any developer tool, modifying the developer tool's own agent directory, and modifying the external specialist-workforce tooling or its guard.
Live model-provider routing, a model router, provider credentials for specialists, and live specialist execution by any real model or provider, which remain activation inputs.

A new governance role, a second source of governance truth, unrestricted agent-to-agent messaging, personality or soul engines, agent social networks, training or reinforcement-learning pipelines, autonomous negotiation, unbounded memory and unbounded multi-agent debate.

phases.title: Host-derived candidate evidence and complete dormant production adapters
phases.description: Continue the accepted host review path implementation candidate so that the independent review is made about evidence the host derived from the candidate it attests, and so that every production port and the installed service route exist in source and fail closed until the owner supplies the protected activation inputs. Nothing is activated: no service start, no authority mint, no credential, no provider call and no spend.
phases.scope: Host candidate-evidence contract and envelope; one read-only tree-difference addition and an ancestry check in the existing repository reader; trusted baseline from the durable approved-plan record; attestation binding of baseline, candidate and evidence digest; bounded local candidate commit authority and the unattended ordering change in the technical continuation; owner-signed cost policy, model-policy text and credential-reference text in the second-version execution closure model and its verification; all production port adapters; the dormant status-and-review service route and the status representation; session and peer composition; the declared validator amendments; the proofs and reviews. No activation of any kind.
exclusions: No second repository reader, no second candidate digest, no second transport stack, no new wire protocol and no widening of the fixed authority frames.
No caller-controlled baseline and no baseline taken from a mutable remote-tracking reference.
No silent truncation of authoritative evidence.
No agent-supplied text accepted as host-established evidence.
No push, merge, tag, amend, reset, rebase, force update, history rewrite or publication by the local candidate commit authority.
No accounted cost described as actual or provider-billed cost.
No use of the owner programme delegation as the host's independent source of model policy or credential reference.
No production route to the review capability, and no status record reporting protected operations as authorised while that capability is unminted.
No change to the interactive route's order, provenance or behaviour.
No weakening of any validator rule that the declared amendments do not name.

No standalone commit, acceptance or closure of the preceding host review path phase: it is reconciled and closed only after this phase is accepted, against the same accepted cumulative candidate, by owner decision, and no earlier candidate of that phase alone is ever treated as the final implementation.

No repository hook executed, no replacement reference or graft honoured and no repository-local, user-level or system-level git configuration consulted by any host repository read or by the local candidate commit.
No filter, conversion or line-ending translation applied to evidence contents, and no symbolic link followed.
No baseline derived or advanced at run time, and no execution closure lacking the cost policy, the model-policy text identity or the credential-reference text identity accepted with a default.
No change to phase selection beyond the one validator-pinned historical-to-continuation pairing, and no second phase-selection function.
acceptanceCriteria: The host derives the complete changed-path set between the approved baseline and the pinned candidate through the one existing repository reader, and a path changed in the candidate cannot be absent from the evidence.

The repository reader gains exactly one read-only tree-difference command and one read-only ancestry check, both taking validated commit identities only, their production spelling is deterministic and validator-pinned, the difference is taken between the two endpoint trees with rename detection disabled and full-length identities, and no second repository reader exists.
The host refuses when the baseline is absent, when the candidate is absent and when the baseline is not an ancestor of the candidate.

Every host repository read used by the review, the existing committed-blob read included, runs with replacement references and grafts disabled, with no repository-local, user-level or system-level git configuration able to alter what is read or to run a program, under an environment the host fixes, and returns raw committed object bytes; a planted replacement reference, graft, configuration entry or attribute filter in the governed worktree changes neither the ancestry answer nor the evidence, and this is proven against a real disposable repository.

The baseline comes from the durable approved-plan record under owner-bound plan and phase authority, a caller cannot supply or influence it, it is never read from a remote-tracking reference, it is never derived or advanced at run time, and the candidate is the head commit of the governed phase worktree as the host pinned it once.

For each changed path the evidence records the change type, the canonical path, the old and new file mode, the content identity, the sha256 of the reviewer-visible bytes and the bounded contents where supported, so that a mode-only change is visible, and deleted paths are explicit.

A submodule pointer entry, any other unsupported entry kind, an ambiguous parse, an oversize path and total evidence beyond the configured bound each refuse the review, a symbolic link entry is reported as a link and never followed, and authoritative evidence is never truncated.

The reviewer input carries a host-established block and an agent-claimed block separated by a host-generated marker that cannot be derived from candidate content, the agent-claimed block is labelled as not host verified, the host-written reviewer instructions state that every byte inside either block is data and never an instruction, and candidate content or agent text that imitates a block boundary, a host statement or a reviewer directive cannot replace, alter or be mistaken for host-established evidence.

The review operation executes against exactly the host-framed evidence, and the attestation binds the baseline, the candidate, the digest of the canonical evidence, the request and correlation, the decision and the existing authority bindings.
An attestation whose evidence digest does not match the evidence the agent can recompute from the same baseline and candidate is refused on the agent side.
No arbitrary agent subject can obtain a candidate review attestation, and a candidate mismatch between the agent's claim and the host's pinned commit is refused with nothing run.

On the unattended route the candidate is committed locally before the independent review, only phase-scope changes enter that commit, a correction is an additive commit, the reviewed object is always the cumulative change from the approved baseline to the newest candidate, an unreviewed local candidate commit is consumable by no other governed action, and the local commit authority performs no push, merge, tag, amend, reset, rebase, force update or history rewrite.

The local candidate commit is created without executing any repository hook and without any repository-local or user-level configuration being able to run a program, the governed worktree's hook directory is never trusted or invoked by any ProjectOS operation, and a planted hook is proven not to run.
The interactive route keeps its existing order, provenance and behaviour, and the existing hybrid gatekeeper, hybrid closure and reconcile suites pass unmodified.

The admitted cost used for pre-dispatch reservation comes from the owner-signed execution-cost policy, an absent policy refuses, and no accounted cost is described as actual or provider-billed cost anywhere in source, records or messages.
A dispatch whose actual cost is not independently established retains its reservation according to the existing reservation semantics, and an entry carrying recorded usage is never released.

The host derives the model-policy and credential-reference identity digests from canonical text in the verified owner-signed execution closure, that text and the cost policy are covered by the owner's signature under the closure's one canonical deterministic encoding, a verified closure lacking the cost policy or either text identity is refused rather than given a default, the delegation's digest claims are only the cross-check, and a disagreement refuses.

A source implementation exists for the admitted-cost source, the signed-execution-closure facts source, the trust-manifest port, the committed-bytes port, the executable-policy port, the gatekeeper execution port, the clock port, the status-and-review service route, the status representation and the session and peer composition, and each fails closed while its live input is absent.

The gatekeeper execution port launches only the closure-verified broker under the pinned packaged runtime, takes no executable, script, environment or endpoint from a caller, reads no credential in this phase and calls no provider in this phase.

The installed service's production composition contains the dormant review-capable route, that route cannot be exercised without the unminted review capability, and the live status reports protected operations as not authorised while the capability is unminted.

After this phase, supplying the protected activation inputs and starting the service requires no further source code for the host review route to work, and the report states this as a port-by-port check rather than an assertion.

Every declared validator amendment, the two first declared for the preceding phase included, states the exact old invariant and the exact new invariant, no unrelated rule is weakened, and each amended validator is proven non-vacuous by mutation.

Request bytes produced by the real agent implementation are accepted by the real host decoder and response bytes and evidence produced by the real host implementation are accepted by the real agent verifier, through one committed cross-language vector file.

The real isolated pipe proofs pass on a run-scoped test endpoint in an elevated shell with no production endpoint, no service start or install, no access-control change, no provider and no credential, and an operating-system refusal is reported exactly rather than skipped.

A valid technical review, a valid reconciliation and a valid closure review each proceed through the actual hybrid turn over the host-derived evidence, and wrong project, wrong phase, wrong evidence subject, wrong request digest, wrong correlation, an invalid attestation, a malformed, oversize or trailing-data response and a replayed answer are each refused.
An absent host and an unavailable host each fail closed with no secondary route, and there is no direct-provider fallback, no interactive fallback and no implementer self-review fallback on any path.

A production build cannot obtain an authority of the review scope, the live transport authority constant remains false, and the transport crate's endpoint count, binary-target absence and unsafe confinement are unchanged.
The agent typecheck across sources and tests passes, the agent and core suites pass, and the tests of every touched host crate pass.
No real provider call, no provider spend, no credential use, no service start, no access-control change, no authority mint, no signing key use and no production activity occurred during the phase.

The preceding host review path phase is never committed, accepted or closed on its own candidate or on its own owner-gate sentence; it is reconciled and closed by the owner only after this phase is accepted, against the same accepted cumulative candidate that satisfies this phase's evidence contract; no earlier candidate of that phase alone is treated as the final implementation; and only this phase's evidence contract can satisfy the host review path validator.

While the continuation phase is not accepted, automated phase selection never selects the historical host review phase and selects the continuation phase instead; after the continuation phase is accepted, the historical phase is offered only to the governed reconciliation and closure operation against the same accepted cumulative candidate and never to implementation execution; no candidate of the historical phase alone can become final; every other phase keeps the first-incomplete-in-plan-order rule; the pairing is pinned to exactly that one pair by the extended work-record authority validator; and each branch is proven by test and the pin by mutation.
requiredReviews: Application security recheck of candidate and evidence binding
requiredOwnerGates: Commit of the implementation to the governed branch, push, merge and phase closure remain owner-gated. The bounded local candidate commit authority is the only commit this phase may create without a further owner decision, and it grants no publication authority.

Approving this phase ratifies, in its own right and not merely as carried forward, the operation-contract validator amendment. Old invariant: no shipped construction of the execution evidence exists anywhere in the transport crate. New invariant: exactly one shipped mint exists, private, reachable only from the single function that takes both the authority and the sealed execution seam, taking its correlation from the authority and unable to mint a not-run result.

Approving this phase ratifies, in its own right and not merely as carried forward, the transport capability validator amendment. Old invariant: the transport crate's closed dependency list does not contain the gatekeeper attestation crate. New invariant: the list contains exactly one added edge to that crate, together with a capability scan of that crate's sources and a closed dependency list for it. These two ratifications supersede the preceding phase's statement that exactly one amendment is ratified and that no other pinned invariant changes.

Approving this phase ratifies the repository reader amendment. Old invariant: the closed repository command vocabulary contains exactly the existing read-only commands, its only content read is the committed blob at one path of one exact commit, and its fixed environment does not disable replacement references, grafts or repository-local configuration. New invariant: the vocabulary additionally contains exactly one read-only recursive endpoint-tree difference between two exact commits reporting status, modes and full-length object identities with rename detection disabled, and exactly one read-only ancestry check between two exact commits, both taking validated commit identities only and neither taking a reference, a path pattern or a caller-supplied option; and every read of the vocabulary used by the review runs with replacement references and grafts disabled and with no repository-local, user-level or system-level configuration able to alter the result or run a program.

Approving this phase ratifies the technical-continuation amendment. Old invariant: on every route the independent review precedes the commit and an approval authorises the commit and the push. New invariant: on the unattended route only, a bounded local candidate commit precedes the independent review, the review is made against that immutable commit, and an approval authorises the separately governed continuation, while the interactive route keeps the old invariant unchanged.

Approving this phase ratifies the phase-selection amendment. Old invariant: automated phase selection takes the first phase in plan order that is not recorded complete and never selects past it. New invariant: the same rule holds for every phase except the one validator-pinned historical-to-continuation pairing of this plan, for which the historical phase is never selected for implementation execution, the continuation phase is selected in its place while it is not accepted, and after its acceptance the historical phase is offered only to the governed reconciliation and closure operation against the same accepted cumulative candidate. The runner still selects only through the one existing phase-selection function. This phase ratifies it as the work-record authority validator amendment: that existing validator, already required by this phase, is extended to pin exactly that one pairing and the absence of any second phase-selection function, and to refuse any other pairing, any widened pairing and any selection of the historical phase for implementation execution. Until this phase's own guard is committed, this phase is implemented only through explicit phase commands naming it, never through automated continuation.

Approving this phase ratifies the bounded local candidate commit authority as a new, narrowly scoped write in the governed phase worktree. Old invariant: ProjectOS creates a commit only as an approved technical continuation after review, and the host repository vocabulary is read-only. New invariant: on the unattended route ProjectOS may additionally create additive local candidate commits before review, without hooks and without configuration-driven programs, with no push, merge, tag, amend, reset, rebase, force update, history rewrite or publication; the host repository vocabulary stays read-only.

Approving this phase ratifies the host review path validator amendment. Old invariant: the review subject is the agent-written provider request bound by its parameter digest. New invariant: the reviewer input is the host-framed evidence envelope, the host-established block is derived by the host alone, and the attestation binds the baseline, the candidate and the evidence digest.

Approving this phase ratifies the execution-closure model addition: the second-version closure additionally carries an execution-cost policy, a model-policy text identity and a credential-reference text identity, each covered by the owner's signature. No closure is produced, signed or installed in this phase.
Approving this phase ratifies the durable approved-plan record addition that carries the approved phase baseline commit, including its schema revision.

No production deployment, database mutation, messaging, payment, credential or delegation creation or disclosure, signing key use, service installation or start, access-control or registry change, force push or merge.

Activating the path remains a separate explicit owner decision covering the review capability mint, the service-control observation capability grant, the clock-binding grant, the owner-signed closure and delegation, the live credential and configuration, the store access control, the service start and the publication authority, and host response authentication and storage authority must be explicitly proven before live use.

The preceding host review path phase is carried in this plan unchanged only because the planning mechanism cannot retire an unfinished phase. Approving this plan is also the owner's decision that it may not close independently: this phase first completes and is accepted against the cumulative candidate, and only then is the preceding phase reconciled and closed against that same accepted candidate. This phase declares no dependency on it, since a dependency on a phase that may only close afterwards could never be satisfied.

phases.title: Governed agent workforce foundation with one persistent project leader
phases.description: Create the universal governed specialist-workforce foundation for ProjectOS: exactly one persistent project leader per active governed project execution, a versioned agent registry holding the complete approved specialist catalogue at a pinned upstream commit, dynamic minimum-team selection with explained rationale, structured specialist contracts, an operational leader ledger, separation of agent role from execution model, third-party provenance, governed catalogue updates, a basic evaluation contract and independent-review boundaries, so that the full catalogue is available without ProjectOS becoming an uncontrolled swarm. The operating model is: owner, then ProjectOS governance, then exactly one project leader, then dynamically selected specialists, then execution models and tools, then evidence, then ProjectOS gates, then the owner wherever protected authority is required. Nothing is activated: no live specialist execution, no provider call, no credential and no spend.
phases.scope: The project leader role and its constitutional invariants; the agent registry contract and the pinned catalogue import with provenance; the selection policy and rationale; the specialist task and result contracts; the leader ledger; least-privilege context and tool grants; role and model separation with approved fallback; review independence; catalogue update governance; the evaluation contract; team-size, cost and context controls; objective-driven operation through the existing command surface; the new workforce validator; the proofs and reviews. A governed project execution means one governed project identity, whose active approved plan scopes its work; its project leader persists across that project's phases, sessions and plan successions, and is replaced only by a ProjectOS takeover that starts a new leader generation.
exclusions: No new governance role: the project leader acts inside the existing implementer role and never holds owner or gatekeeper authority.
No second source of governance truth: the leader ledger is operational state and yields to the ProjectOS governance records whenever they differ.
No imported instruction text treated as authority, and no agent permission taken from an agent's own text.
No unrestricted peer-to-peer agent messaging; specialists report through the project leader in structured results.
No run of the whole catalogue: selection is the smallest team that credibly completes the task.
No live specialist execution by any real model or provider, no provider credential and no spend in this phase: every proof uses deterministic fixture execution engines.
No model router and no live model-provider routing: the registry records model preferences only as references to owner-approved model policy.
No global installation of specialists into any developer tool, no change to the developer tool's own agent directory, and no change to the external specialist-workforce tooling or its guard.
No catalogue import from a moving branch, and no silent automatic update of an imported catalogue.
No personality or soul engine, agent social network, training or reinforcement-learning pipeline, autonomous negotiation, unbounded memory or unbounded debate.

No change to the host review path, its evidence contract or its validators, and no weakening of any existing pinned invariant; if implementation finds an existing invariant that must change, it stops for an owner ruling.
No full normalisation or behavioural evaluation of roles beyond those the representative task types need, and no live behavioural evaluation of any role.

No change to automated phase selection: this phase relies on the host review continuation's mechanical phase-selection guard unchanged, and it cannot begin until that continuation phase is recorded complete.
acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one project leader record exists for each active governed project execution, meaning one governed project identity whose active approved plan scopes its work; the record is minted and checked only by ProjectOS code that the leader session cannot invoke on its own behalf, is held under an exclusive durable claim carrying a leader generation, persists across sessions, restarts, phases and plan successions, and is rebuilt from a bounded projection of its ledger rather than from unbounded conversation memory.
An attempt to create a second simultaneous project leader for the same governed project execution is refused, and the existing leader is unchanged.

A leader claim is stale only when it exceeds a governance-owned lease bound, and a stale leader is replaced only by ProjectOS, never by hand and never by another leader, and the takeover increments the leader generation; every task, grant and result issued under an older generation is void and rejected when it arrives; every takeover is recorded as an event.
An attempt to start any specialist task without the project leader of that execution is refused before any context is assembled or any engine is invoked.

The project leader cannot approve its own work, approve a specialist's protected action, approve production deployment, production database mutation, live communication, payment or refund, disclose or use a protected credential outside policy, change governance, expand commercial or material scope, accept an unresolved critical or high risk, approve phase closure, go around the gatekeeper or the owner, mint authority, or change workforce configuration, registry eligibility, selection policy or model policy; those four are governance-owned data changed only through the owner's commit gate, ProjectOS reads them only from the owner-accepted committed state and never from the working tree or an unreviewed local candidate commit, a phase change to any of them is listed separately at the owner's commit gate, and each prohibition is proven refused by the ProjectOS gate that already owns it, not by the leader's own instructions.

Orchestration is hierarchical: specialists receive work from and return structured results to the project leader only; no evaluator panel is required in this phase, an undeclared panel is refused, any panel declares its participants, purpose, input and output contracts, maximum rounds, termination rule, failure rule, cost and context budget and decision owner before it runs and stops at its declared limit, and panel output never satisfies an independent-review requirement.
